meta.title: Vascularization ability of glioma stem cells in different three-dimensional microenvironments.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Glioma stem cells were printed in a gelatin/alginate scaffold and compared with other 3D settings to study how they form blood vessels. Printed cells stayed about 85% viable over a week.

formulations.name: 10% gelatin + 1% alginate (glioma stem cells)
formulations.key_outcome: Printed GSCs were 86.7% viable on day 1 and 85.3% on day 7, steadier than a cast hybrid hydrogel (65% by day 7).

evidence.quote: to reach a final concentration of 10% gelatin, 1% sodium alginate and 2 × 105/ml GSC23 cells
the cell viability of GSCs in 3D bioprinted hydrogel scaffold and hybrid hydrogel was 86.65 ± 1.64% and 92.71 ± 1.33%, respectively
GSC models were generated using an extrusion bioprinter (Medprin Regenerative Medical Technologies Co., Ltd., Guangzhou, China)
